Class 2 · Chapter 9 of 9

Codes, hidden shapes and order

Find the odd one out, read simple codes, spot hidden shapes and find places in a row.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Read picture charts. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can group pictures and use an analogy.
  • I can use a code key to read a message.
  • I can find an exact shape hidden in a picture.
  • I can find a place in a row.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Odd one out

Look for what most pictures share. Then find the one that is different.

The cube and the cuboid have flat faces. The sphere is round, so it is the odd one out.

Screen 2 of 5

Use the same rule

Small circle goes with big circle. So small square goes with big square.

The rule is: the second picture is bigger.

Screen 3 of 5

Read a code

A code key says what each symbol means. A is 1, B is 2 and C is 3.

So C A B in code is 3 1 2.

Screen 4 of 5

Find a hidden shape

A small shape can hide inside a bigger picture.

Find the exact shape, with the same size and turn. Here an L-shape hides in the corner.

Screen 5 of 5

Find a place in a row

There are 8 children in a row. Mia is 3rd from the left.

Counting from the right, Mia is 6th. The place depends on which end you start from.

Words to know
odd one out
The one that does not belong with the others.
code
A secret way of writing. A key says what each symbol means.
1st, 2nd, 3rd
Words for position in a row: first, second, third.

For parents

What your child learns

Reasoning is thinking clearly about clues. Your child sorts, matches a rule to a new picture, reads a simple code and says who is 1st, 2nd or 3rd in a row.

A common slip

Children often count from the wrong end of a row. Ask: "Which end are we counting from?" Also check that a hidden shape is the same size, not just similar.

5-minute home activity: Odd one out at home

  1. Put three spoons and one fork on the table.
  2. Ask which one is the odd one out and why.
  3. Now line up 5 toys. Ask who is 2nd from the left and who is 2nd from the right.
